questions.q: A passenger collapses inside a moving train. The operator's first action is to:
options: Stop the train immediately between stations
Inform Operations Control Centre (OCC) so that the station where help will wait is ready with first aid and a wheelchair/stretcher
Ask fellow passengers to complete the treatment
Speed up to reach the final destination
questions.explain: Advance information turns a platform into a prepared medical point — stopping in a section traps the patient.

questions.q: In a medical emergency on a train, the patient is usually taken off at:
options: Whichever station comes first, ready or not
The depot, at the end of the trip
The station where medical help has been arranged to meet the train
The station nearest the passenger's home
questions.explain: Operations Control Centre (OCC) balances patient urgency against trapping a full train in a section — help waits at a chosen station.

questions.q: Who arranges the ambulance for a medical emergency reported from a train?
options: Operations Control Centre (OCC)/station control, to meet the train at the designated station
The patient himself, after detraining
The train operator, from the cab phone directory
The catering staff on board
questions.explain: Coordination is centralised — the ambulance is sent to the right station before the train arrives.

questions.q: What should the receiving station keep ready at the exact coach position?
options: A ticket refund counter
The station master's office keys
Refreshments for the patient
Wheelchair, stretcher and the first-aid team
questions.explain: Knowing the coach position saves minutes — help waits at the door the patient will use.

questions.q: First aid for a collapsed passenger should be given by:
options: Any passenger who volunteers, however untrained
The youngest passenger available
Trained staff or first responders, until medical help takes over
Nobody — first aid is only for hospitals
questions.explain: Trained first aid bridges the gap until the ambulance crew arrives.

questions.q: A train carrying a serious patient is approaching the designated station. The train should be held there:
options: Only as long as needed to hand the patient over safely
For a fixed one hour in every case
Until the patient fully recovers on board
Not at all — the patient must jump quickly
questions.explain: The hold is measured by the handover, not by a fixed rule — patient first, but the line must flow again.

questions.q: When a patient is handed over to medical help, staff should pass on:
options: The patient's ticket for refund
A note of what happened, when, and what first aid was given
The train's delay statement
Nothing — the doctors will guess
questions.explain: A written note of events and treatment given helps the medical team continue care without gaps.

questions.q: Which passenger evacuation triggers are correct for a station?
options: Rain outside the station
A train running five minutes late
A passenger losing a ticket
Fire, smoke, bomb threat or security direction, structural emergency, or a crowd emergency
questions.explain: Evacuation is for threats to life or safety — not for weather or routine delays.

questions.q: The first announcement in a station evacuation must clearly state:
options: What has happened, where to go, and what NOT to do
The commercial offers in station shops
The full history of the incident
Only the station name, repeatedly
questions.explain: People act on three things: the problem, the route, and the forbidden actions (like using lifts in a fire).

questions.q: During a station evacuation, after opening exits, staff must also:
options: Lock all side rooms immediately
Sweep toilets and side rooms so nobody is left behind
Check the ticket gates' cash
Switch off all station lighting
questions.explain: A sweep finds the person in the toilet or rest room who never heard the announcement.

questions.q: Passengers with disabilities or limited mobility are evacuated using:
options: The normal crowd flow without any help
Lifts, in all circumstances including fire
Evacuation chairs and refuge points, with staff assistance
Goods trolleys from the parcels office
questions.explain: Evacuation chairs and refuge points exist exactly for those who cannot use stairs quickly.

questions.q: The 'all-clear' after a station evacuation can be given only by:
options: The authorised command, after checks and headcount are complete
Any staff member who feels it is safe
The passengers waiting outside
The operator of the next arriving train
questions.explain: Re-entry is a formal decision — it follows accounting, not feelings.

questions.q: In a crowd emergency on a platform, the very first control action is to:
options: Push the crowd towards the platform edge
Open more entry gates to relieve the gates
Ask passengers to run to the trains
Stop further entry into the station/platform
questions.explain: Adding more people to a crush makes it worse — entry stops before anything else.

questions.q: A platform is dangerously crowded at one end. Relief should begin at:
options: The emptiest point first
The densest point first
The ticket counter
The station entrance only
questions.explain: Pressure is relieved where it can hurt people — the densest point is the danger point.

questions.q: During an evacuation, a crowd flow must never be:
options: Pushed against an incoming evacuation flow moving the opposite way
Guided by staff at junctions
Slowed at narrow gates
Counted at the assembly point
questions.explain: Opposing flows lock and crush — evacuation routes are one-direction systems.

questions.q: A person has fallen onto the track from a platform. Staff should first:
options: Jump onto the track at once to pull him out
Shout to the person to climb up unaided
Operate the emergency stop facility where provided and inform Operations Control Centre (OCC) to stop trains and arrange power protection
Film the incident for the enquiry
questions.explain: Stop the danger first — trains and power. Track entry for rescue needs authority and protection.

questions.q: Why must nobody enter the track for a rescue without authority and power protection?
options: The track is cleaned only at night
Rescue is a police-only job in all cases
The timetable does not allow it
A rescuer on a live track becomes a second casualty
questions.explain: Unprotected rescue attempts multiply casualties — protection first, then rescue.

questions.q: A medical emergency occurs on a crowded platform. Along with first aid, staff must:
options: Clear space around the patient and inform Operations Control Centre (OCC)/station control for an ambulance
Move the patient through the crowd to the exit at once
Announce the patient's name and illness to everyone
Stop all trains in the network for the day
questions.explain: Space, first aid and an arranged ambulance — the platform version of the same system.

questions.q: A passenger feels unwell and dizzy on a train but is conscious. The sensible course is:
options: Ignore it as it is not an emergency at all
Inform Operations Control Centre (OCC), seat and monitor him, and detrain him at a station where staff can help if needed
Stop the train in the section immediately
Ask him to stand near the door for air
questions.explain: Not every case needs a section stop — information, monitoring and a prepared station cover most.

questions.q: During a passenger evacuation, who guides flows at stairs, gates and junctions?
options: Only the station master, alone
Passengers who know the station well
Positioned staff at each key point
Nobody — crowds sort themselves out
questions.explain: Guidance at choke points is what keeps an evacuation moving instead of jamming.

questions.q: An evacuation is ordered due to a bomb threat. Passengers should be moved:
options: As directed by security/police, away from the threatened area, without touching suspicious objects
Towards the object to identify it
Only after their tickets are checked
Into the nearest train for shelter
questions.explain: Security threats run on police direction — distance and not touching anything are the life-savers.

questions.q: At the assembly point after evacuation, the essential activity is:
options: Distributing refreshments first
Allowing everyone to leave immediately
Collecting feedback forms
Headcount — confirming every person is accounted for
questions.explain: The headcount is the proof of a completed evacuation.

questions.q: A wheelchair user is on an upper floor during a station fire evacuation. The correct method is:
options: Carry him down in his wheelchair by two passengers
Move him to a refuge point and evacuate with an evacuation chair by trained staff
Use the lift as a special exception
Leave him and inform the fire brigade of the floor only
questions.explain: Refuge points and evacuation chairs are the planned method — lifts stay forbidden in fire.

questions.q: Why are emergency gates opened during a station evacuation instead of using only the normal gates?
options: Emergency gates are closer to the shops
Normal gates must be preserved for revenue
Normal gates are too narrow and slow for a full crowd leaving at once
Emergency gates are opened for practice only
questions.explain: Evacuation speed depends on exit width — emergency gates remove the bottleneck.

questions.q: A train is held at a station for a medical case and other passengers grow restless. The crew should:
options: Keep them informed — reason for the hold and expected delay
Refuse to give any reason
Blame the sick passenger by name
Ask restless passengers to leave the station
questions.explain: Information keeps a held train calm — the same rule as in a train failure.

questions.q: A passenger is found unconscious in a station toilet during a fire evacuation sweep. Staff should:
options: Lock the toilet and continue the sweep
Wait for him to wake up
Note it for the end-of-shift report only
Raise the alarm, move him to safety with help if possible, and report his condition and location
questions.explain: The sweep exists to find exactly this person — he is rescued and reported, never left.

questions.q: In a medical emergency, why does Operations Control Centre (OCC) prefer detraining the patient at a planned station rather than stopping in the section?
options: Section stops are against the timetable only
Patients recover faster at stations
In a section there is no platform, no stretcher access and no ambulance reach
Ambulances are not allowed near tracks by law in any case
questions.explain: Everything a patient needs exists at a station and nothing exists in a section.

questions.q: Which is a correct pairing for evacuation assistance priority?
options: Season-ticket holders — first
Children, elderly, pregnant women and persons with disabilities — first
Passengers with the largest luggage — first
Staff families — first
questions.explain: Vulnerability, not ticket class, decides who is helped first.

questions.q: After a station evacuation ends, the incident record must show:
options: Trigger, actions taken, headcount result and the all-clear authority
Only the number of trains delayed
The names of passengers who complained
The day's weather report
questions.explain: The record proves the evacuation was completed and accounted — part of the safety loop.

questions.q: A serious medical case is reported from a train two stations away from a major hospital interchange. Operations Control Centre (OCC) will most likely:
options: Order an immediate section stop
Cancel the patient's journey at the next small station without help
Arrange the ambulance and team at the interchange station and direct the train there
Ask the patient to travel to the hospital by himself later
questions.explain: Help is placed where it is strongest — the train goes to the arranged medical point.

questions.q: In serious injuries, the 'golden hour' idea means the railway's medical response should aim at:
options: Completing all paperwork within one hour
Getting the patient to proper medical care as fast as possible — outcomes are best when treatment starts within the first hour
Waiting one hour to see if the patient recovers
Holding the train for one full hour
questions.explain: The first hour after a serious injury is when quick treatment saves the most lives. Everything — first aid, stretcher, ambulance — is arranged to beat that clock.

questions.q: A passenger is found not breathing and with no pulse. A trained staff member or trained bystander should immediately start:
options: Giving the patient water
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) — chest compressions — and continue until medical help takes over
Moving the patient to a seat
Waiting silently for the ambulance
questions.explain: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) keeps blood moving to the brain when the heart has stopped. Starting it at once, and not stopping till professionals arrive, is the life-saving action.

questions.q: In most Indian states, the free government ambulance service for a medical emergency is summoned on the number:
questions.explain: 108 is the emergency ambulance number in most Indian states (112 is the combined emergency number). Stations keep these numbers ready — searching for them during an emergency wastes the golden time.

questions.q: A patient with a suspected spinal (back or neck) injury should generally:
options: Be carried quickly by his arms and legs
Not be moved except by trained medical staff with proper support, unless he is in immediate danger where he lies
Be made to sit up and drink water
Be walked to the first-aid room to keep him awake
questions.explain: Moving a spinal injury wrongly can cause permanent paralysis. Keep the patient still and supported, protect him from further harm, and let the trained medical team shift him.

questions.q: Passengers are being detrained onto the track because the train cannot move. Before anyone steps down, the most important protection is:
options: Checking that all passengers have their luggage
Stopping or cautioning trains on the adjacent (other) line and posting staff to guide passengers to a safe place clear of all tracks
Switching off the station lights
Announcing the train's next departure time
questions.explain: The biggest danger in track detrainment is a train on the other line. That line is protected first, and passengers are led along a safe route away from every track.
